newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish refineries raise petrol prices.
newsitem.headline: Polish refineries raise petrol prices.

text.p: Poland's two largest fuel producers, Petrochemia Plock SA and Rafineria Gdanska SA, have raised petrol prices by between 0.01 and 0.03 zloty per litre, the companies said on Tuesday.
But the country's largest fuel distribution network CPN said it would not raise prices for at least one week as it was still selling fuel bought at a discount.
"On July 22 we removed discounts introduced in June, which caused petrol price to rise about 0.01 zlotys on average," Petrochemia refinery spokeswoman Romana Kuffel said.
She said the price of diesel remained unchanged.
The increase was necessary because a weaker zloty exchange rate made imported crude oil more expensive, Kuffel added.
Rafineria Gdanska's spokeswoman said the company would also scrap its price discount on Wednesday.
"Tomorrow Rafineria will lift its price discount introduced on June 25, which amounted to 30 zlotys per tonne of 94-octane and unleaded petrol," Ewa Sielicka said.
The 30 zlotys per tonne discount is equivalent to about 0.03 zloty per litre.
CPN official Barbara Hotbot told Reuters that the company still had some petrol in stock and it was not going to raise prices within the coming week.

Hotbot said that fuel prices, depending on the region, ranged from 1.68 to 1.74 zlotys for 94-octane petrol, 1.63 to 1.73 for 95-octane petrol, 1.79 to 1.85 for unleaded petrol and 1.36 to 1.42 for diesel.
